subject: Deployment mode follow-up: SSO, KMS/HSM, and logging retention
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.inference, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.inference
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment mode follow-up: SSO, KMS/HSM, and logging retention

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for taking the call today — great to learn more about FintechCo's use cases and latency/throughput targets. As discussed, I wanted to summarize the items that will determine the best deployment mode (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC/on-prem) and confirm next steps.

Quick summary of your stated constraints:
- SSO: SAML/SCIM integration with Azure AD (company-wide provisioning and role-based access)
- KMS/HSM: Customer-managed keys required; prefer AWS KMS with external key material or HSM-backed key wrapping
- Logging: Audit logs and request-level logs retained for up to 7 years and pushed into FintechCo SIEM (Splunk) via a secure forwarder
- Data residency: US-only region for inference and logs

How these map to deployment modes (high level):
- Hosted API: fast to get started but typically cannot meet customer-managed KMS/HSM or long-term on-prem log retention requirements. Logs are retained by Redwood per our standard retention and export policies (we can discuss extensions).
- Dedicated: Reserved GPU pools with VPC peering/PrivateLink can address some isolation and egress requirements; KMS integration is possible but may require a longer onboarding window and special configuration for external key material. Long-term (7yr) retention and SIEM forwarding can often be accommodated via customer-managed log sinks, but we'd need to validate retention SLAs with our infra team.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): Full control model — supports SAML/SCIM SSO integration, direct KMS/HSM integration, and customer-managed log retention/forwarding. This is usually the route customers pick when they have strict KMS and retention requirements.

Next steps I propose:
1) Quick technical call (30–45m) with your security/infra lead + our infra SE (Rishi) and solutions engineer (Vivek) to validate KMS/HSM and logging integration details.
2) I'll send a short pre-call checklist (items below) and attach a one-pager comparing deployment modes.
3) If Private is required, we'll follow with an internal sizing + timeline estimate and draft PoC plan.

Pre-call checklist (please confirm availability):
- Which KMS provider/version (AWS KMS, customer key material, HSM vendor) and whether key import is required
- Expected request volume / tokens per second for peak traffic
- SIEM endpoint details and log format requirements (syslog, HTTPS ingestion, Kafka, etc.)
- Any regulatory controls that mandate on-premise only deployments

I've attached a short compare_deployment_modes.pdf to this thread. Are you available for a call Wed or Thu this week? I can send a few slots.

Best,

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: compare_deployment_modes.pdf (one-pager)

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Cc: security@fintechco.com
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment mode follow-up: SSO, KMS/HSM, and logging retention

Marissa,

Thanks for the recap — that aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side that will drive the decision:

1) SSO: We run Azure AD with SAML 2.0 for SSO and SCIM for provisioning. Need SCIM user/group sync + role mapping for admin vs read-only roles.

2) KMS/HSM: We require customer-managed keys. Ideally AWS KMS with imported key material or an HSM-backed key wrap where Redwood never has access to the plaintext keys. We also use CloudHSM in some accounts.

3) Logging & retention: 7 years for audit logs by policy. Logs need to be forwarded into our Splunk cluster over a secure channel; we use persistent storage in our logging account for long-term retention. We cannot rely on vendor short retention windows.

4) Data residency: All inference and logs must remain in the US commercial region (no EU/APAC copies).

Given the above, Hosted API looks unlikely unless there's a bespoke agreement around KMS and retention. Dedicated could work if you can: (a) support AWS KMS with imported key material or CloudHSM, (b) provide a customer-managed log sink or VPC-based forwarding to our SIEM, and (c) guarantee data residency. Private would be preferred if Dedicated cannot meet the KMS/HSM guarantee.

Attaching our security questionnaire (partially filled) and SOC2 pointer. Also, procurement is sensitive to deployment model because of the compliance review — useful to align now.

Regards,
Alex

--
Alex Johnson
CTO | FintechCo
alex.johnson@fintechco.com
(650) 555-0199

Attachment: SOC2-report-2025.pdf

Subject: Re: Deployment mode follow-up: SSO, KMS/HSM, and logging retention

Alex — thanks for the detailed responses and for the attachments. This is exactly the level of detail we need.

A few operational notes and proposed next steps:

- KMS/HSM: Rishi and Vivek will validate which of our Dedicated configurations can support AWS KMS with imported key material and CloudHSM wrapping. Short answer: we do have customers using Dedicated with CMKs and CloudHSM, but the setup requires an SE-led onboarding (network peering, key policies, and audit proofing).

- Logs & retention: We can route logs out of the Dedicated environment to a customer-managed S3 or log-forwarder in your logging account using VPC peering / PrivateLink. Long-term retention is something we can architect (e.g., direct-to-S3 lifecycle policies you manage for 7 years). For Hosted API, custom 7-year retention is not supported today.

- Data residency: We can pin Dedicated capacity to US regions and ensure no EU/APAC copies. Private will give you the most control here.

Can we schedule a 45m technical deep-dive Thursday, Jul 2 at 09:00 or 14:00 PT? Rishi (infra SE) will walk through KMS/HSM key flows and Vivek (solutions) will cover networking/log forwarding and timeline. Please let me know which slot works or propose alternatives.

Pre-call ask (to make the session efficient):
- Confirm the KMS option you prefer (imported key material vs CloudHSM)
- Provide a sample Splunk ingestion endpoint / protocol (syslog/HTTP/Kafka)
- Provide an estimate of peak qps or tokens/sec and expected growth (helps with sizing)

If Thursday doesn't work, we can do Fri morning.

Thanks — I'll upload the compare_deployment_modes.pdf to the HubSpot record and include the SOC2 pointer you sent.

Best,

--

Quick answers to the pre-call asks:
- We prefer AWS KMS with imported key material if possible; CloudHSM is acceptable as an alternative for key wrapping.
- Splunk ingestion: HTTPS Event Collector (HEC) with token-based auth, endpoint will be provided before the call.
- Peak: approx 120 requests/sec at peak right now, planning for 2x growth over 12 months.

I've attached the completed security questionnaire and SOC2 report for your review. Procurement timeline: 6–8 weeks post technical validation assuming Dedicated can be validated; longer if Private is required. Deal scope is currently small PoC first, then expansion.
